tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). # Construction Intelligence Engine — Implementation Plan

Status: Proposed v0.1
Depends on: `docs/CONSTRUCTION_INTELLIGENCE_SPEC.md`
Reference project: 101 Meydenbauer, Building B

## 0. Delivery strategy

Build this as a sequence of **vertical proofs**, not horizontal infrastructure layers.

Each milestone must leave Meydenbauer more useful than before. Avoid a long rewrite in which the current bid model stops working while a generalized framework is constructed underneath it.

Governing migration rule:

> **Wrap -> prove -> extract -> generalize.**

The current takeoff, model, schedule, logistics and animation pipeline remains operational until its replacement has passed the same or stronger checks.

---

## 1. Success condition

The first release is successful when one project can move through this chain without separate sources of truth:

```text
source evidence
  -> normalized claims
  -> canonical project state
  -> scenario derivation
  -> geometry + quantities + activities + issues
  -> Blender / GLB / Explorer / report / film
```

The signature demonstration is the Meydenbauer depth question:

`POC depth change -> trench condition -> slab SF -> excavation -> logistics -> schedule implication -> visual decision`

If that chain is real, the architecture is real.

---

## 2. Workstream map

| Workstream | Outcome | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| A. Semantic kernel | stable IDs + typed state + validation | none |
| B. Meydenbauer adapter | existing pipeline emits canonical state | A |
| C. Scenario graph | S1/S2/S3 and depth deltas propagate | A, B |
| D. Blender/GLB bridge | semantic IDs survive visual pipeline | A, B |
| E. Explorer | interactive evidence/quantity/time/risk UI | B, C, D |
| F. Flagship film | 84s decision narrative from same state | B, C, D |
| G. Generalization | second project proves core is not Meydenbauer-specific | A–F |

Workstreams overlap only after their contracts are stable enough to avoid churn.

---

# Milestone 0 — Baseline and freeze

## Goal

Capture what works today before touching architecture.

## Tasks

- Record current `main` commit as the migration baseline.
- Run or document the current Meydenbauer build sequence.
- Snapshot current takeoff totals, model checks, animation checks and known deliverables.
- Inventory all values currently duplicated across `prepare.py`, `takeoff.py`, `build.py`, `schedule.py`, `logistics.py`, `animate.py` and `anim_finish.py`.
- Identify manually typed film/HUD quantities that should eventually come from canonical state.
- Identify every existing object metadata field in the `.glb` and Blender scene.

## Deliverable

`projects/meydenbauer-b/state/baseline.json`

This is not canonical state. It is a migration comparison fixture.

## Acceptance

- Current production scripts remain unchanged.
- Baseline contains the known approximately 312.75 LF total and current model-check population.
- Current 4D checks are enumerated so migration cannot silently weaken them.

## Stop/go question

Can we prove after each later milestone that we have not lost a currently working capability?

---

## Goal

Create the smallest shared library capable of representing the specification without importing Blender.

# Meydenbauer Reference Acceptance

Status: Proposed v0.1
Purpose: Golden-reference acceptance contract for the Construction Intelligence Engine (CIE)

## 1. Why this exists

Architecture is cheap to describe. This document makes it expensive to fake.

CIE is accepted only when it can demonstrate construction reasoning end-to-end on the existing Meydenbauer under-slab re-pipe without weakening the checks already present in the project.

The tests below are product tests, not merely unit tests.

---

## 2. Reference facts to preserve

At the time this acceptance contract was written, the current Meydenbauer deliverables report:

- four ground-floor units: B-101 through B-104;
- approximately 312.75 LF of modeled new under-slab ABS;
- four POC cleanouts/tie-ins;
- approximately 105 LF of 2-inch, 33 LF of 3-inch and 175 LF of 4-inch pipe;
- S1 slab cut: 590 SF;
- S2 slab cut: 686 SF;
- S3 reference slab cut: 991 SF;
- allowance reference: 700 SF;
- S2 base excavation at the 3.5 ft POC-invert assumption: approximately 82.3 bank CY;
- 30 fixture/stack connections in the S2 pit assumption;
- B-104 is the largest unit by modeled pipe length and S2 slab area;
- the current strawman unit-by-unit sequence totals 81.5 working days before holidays and preconstruction;
- current unit order is B-103 -> B-102 -> B-101 -> B-104;
- the existing sequence build includes 92 unit-sequence checks and 44 framing checks.

These values are regression fixtures, not license to hard-code the result.

---

## 3. Acceptance A — Identity and evidence

### Test A1 — Select a modeled pipe

Given a known B-104 pipe element in the canonical state:

- it has a stable `cie_id`;
- Blender geometry carries that ID;
- exported GLB geometry can resolve that ID;
- Explorer selection resolves to exactly one canonical element.

**Pass:** all surfaces agree on identity.

### Test A2 — Trace to source

From the selected pipe, the user can navigate to its claim(s) and evidence locator(s), including the relevant P1.02 reference.

**Pass:** the source can be identified without searching README prose or source code.

### Test A3 — Separate plan and elevation confidence

The selected pipe can express different provenance states for plan position, size and elevation.

# Meydenbauer B-101 — demolition model review (v4 → v4.1)

An experimental run of the review workflow on the recovered B-101 demolition model. v4 executed cleanly
but failed acceptance on two items. v4.1 fixes both through a small patch, and the package's own checks pass on it.
**Result: v4.1 accepted for coordination review only; every route, invert and fitting stays FIELD_VERIFY.**

**Illustrative, not a contract document.** A coordination model traced from plans, not field verified.

![v4.1 frame 083: slab removed, existing cast iron and WC carriers exposed](B101_v41_083.jpg)

| Before (v4, default camera, frame 061) | After (v4.1, review camera) |
|---|---|
| ![v4 frame 061: upper floors hide the work](B101_v4_061_before.jpg) | [050 finish strip-out](B101_v41_050.jpg) · [068 sawcut](B101_v41_068.jpg) · [083 CI exposed](B101_v41_083.jpg) · [089 CI removed](B101_v41_089.jpg) |

How it was built, and the patch itself: [products/b101-review](../../products/b101-review/README.md).

## Acceptance checklist

The checklist is the recovered package's `BLENDER_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`. The v4 column is the earlier
execution's recorded result (recovered `checklist_review.md`); v4.1 is this run, on Blender 5.0.1 with
CPU Cycles.

| Item | v4 | v4.1 | Evidence (v4.1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Preflight, strict build, save, reopen | pass | **pass** | All three runs exit 0 with `--fail-on-warning` |
| A. Phase controller, drivers | pass | **pass** | No invalid drivers or `MEYD_DRIVER_ERROR` at 13 checkpoints |
| B. Slab Boolean evaluated | pass | **pass** | 0 mismatches on a 3-inch grid against the cutter union; slab manifold, 5.5 in |
| B. No cut inside prior-ABS no-demo envelope | **fail** (38 samples, ~2.4 sf) | **pass** (0 of 6,400) | Cutters 001/008 clipped at y = 27.5 ft. The envelope edge is an **assumed** cut limit |
| B. Bend continuity, structural crossing | pass | not re-inspected | Same geometry except the clipped ends; DO_NOT_CUT_STRUCTURE tag retained |
| C. Route, 4→6 in continuity, +18 in lateral | pass | **pass (model only)** | Saved route controls match 6/6, 2/2, 4/4 points. Not re-checked against drawings; QA boards not recovered |
| C. Prior ABS distinct and protected | partial | **pass** | Main trench now stops at the envelope (frames 068–089) |
| D. Demolition sequence 001–089 | pass in cutaways | **pass** | All eight keyframes viewed from the review camera. 038 shows access items starting to move, not yet stored. 089 keeps excavation overlays |
| E. Fittings, traps, carriers, cuts, supports | pass | **pass** | 10 junctions, 7 traps, 7 bends, 2 carriers, 10 supports |
| F. Camera shows B-101 clearly; X-ray does not obscure | **fail** | **pass** | `MEYD_B101_REVIEW_CAMERA` plus a render-only cutaway of upper floors, east/north walls and soil |
| F. No black or blank frames | see inventory | **pass** | Eight frames viewed |
| **G. Outcome** | **REVISION REQUIRED** | **ACCEPTED FOR COORDINATION (experimental)** | Not for fabrication or as-built |

## What still needs a person

- **Envelope boundary:** the prior-repair no-demo envelope is a broad box drawn from the P1.01 cloud. Where
  the trench may actually stop near the prior-ABS tie is a field call.
- **Readability:** in-scene annotation text overlaps and is hard to read in the review view. Fix it before
  any render goes to a scope, PCO or resident notice.

## Rebuild

```bash
uv run bm run meydenbauer-b/b101-review build   # writes build/meydenbauer-b/b101-review/ and these JPEGs
```

The `.blend` is not handed over (about 14 MB). `build` regenerates it at
`build/meydenbauer-b/b101-review/pkg/output/`.

content.content:
January 4–February 11, 2027, and retimes an existing 672-frame animation. Main's
Explorer chains eight activities per unit across four units on an assumed
81.5-working-day S2 baseline. These are structurally different schedules.
Their scope, resource and occupancy assumptions must be compared before their
durations can be treated as alternatives. S1/S3 durations remain not calculated
in the merged Explorer; do not restore the superseded excavation-only duration
sensitivity from closed PR #38.

**Slice 1 (recover data for inspection) is done:** see
[vdc-recovery](../projects/meydenbauer-b/products/vdc-recovery/README.md), with findings in its
[report](../projects/meydenbauer-b/deliverables/vdc-recovery/README.md). 80 text files are byte-identical
to the archive. The scenes and renders stay in the tags. Nothing was imported into the canonical state.

**Slice 2 (owner decisions, 2026-11-05) is done:**
- the B103 raised-floor route is out of scope;
- 40 VDC scope quantities are adopted as assumed;
- the canonical 81.5-working-day schedule governs;
- the seven archived scenes are listed for Releases;
- VDC's 4 open issues are not imported as canonical issues.

See the report's decisions section.

**Slice 3 (close-out, 2026-11-05) is done.** The seven scenes are in release
`meydenbauer-b-vdc-archive-2026-11-05`, and each matches `release-assets.json` by size and sha256.
The archive tags are kept as Git history; the source branches `meydenbauer/4d-fixes` and
`meydenbauer/b101-v4-executed` can be retired.

First recover the small schedule, element, issue, takeoff and route-control data
for inspection. Reconcile identifiers (`vdc_element_id` versus `cie_id`), units,
final-frame quantity methods, evidence and scope coverage against canonical CIE
state. Keep reported VDC slope deviations and unknown slopes explicit. The VDC
README's model and validation claims have not been independently rerun here.

The B101 package contains calibrated route controls and demolition/fitting QA.
Compare these to the main takeoff/spec before importing quantities or replacing
routes. Reuse useful validators; avoid a second canonical state store. Package
large saved models through Releases only after inspecting their external assets.

## Remaining triage

Triaged 2026-11-05 (owner decision):

- `improve-docs-and-reports`: **ported**. `basis_of_record` is required on every spec; `conflicts`,
  `assumptions` and `review` blocks are validated and reported; every render is labelled. See
  [METHOD.md](METHOD.md#spec-record-fields-enforced-by-bm-check-and-bm-build).
- `feat/render-scenes-actions`: **retired**. Its recipe-driven video pipeline used the old layout; the
  installation, immersive and agency films on main replaced it.
- `deliver/highland-archviz-film`: **retired**. It specified a penthouse and terrace not in any drawing.
- `docs/meydenbauer-cutaway-design`: **retired**. Unapproved, never built; it would need a new GPU master.

All four stay recoverable from their `archive/2026-11-03/` tags.

## Validation and future branch practice

At the cleanup baseline, `uv run --no-sync bm check` passed all repository checks,
39 tests and 23 subtests. No historical model builds, product rebuilds or visual
reviews are implied by that result. Recovery PRs must follow [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
including product checks and model/render inspection where applicable.

Use a fresh branch per follow-up, normally targeting main. A stack needs an
explicit integration PR to main. Preserve delivery milestones through tags and
Releases; stop adding commits to branches after their PRs merge. Main protection
and automatic branch deletion are recommendations; repository settings were not
changed in this phase.

The recovery work is finished and nothing is in flight. PR #55, the branch you're on, is merged, as are #56 and #57. There are no open PRs or issues. Your local `main` is behind `origin/main`, so the first step is housekeeping, then a choice between three pieces of work.

**0. Housekeeping (a minute)**
```bash
git switch main && git pull && git branch -d chore/doctor-chromium-libs
```
`docs/BRANCH_RECOVERY.md` also says `meydenbauer/4d-fixes` and `meydenbauer/b101-v4-executed` can be retired, because their archive tags preserve them. I won't delete remote branches unless you say so.

**1. Make the B-101 v4.1 annotations readable (my recommendation)**
The B-101 v4.1 review (#57) was accepted for coordination, but its README lists one item that blocks it from going to anyone: the text annotations in the scene overlap and are hard to read in the review camera. They need fixing before any frame goes into a scope, PCO or resident notice. The scope is small and clear:
- change `products/b101-review/b101_v4_1.patch`
- rebuild in CI, since bpy doesn't run on this laptop
- look at the frames and update the deliverable README

The other open item, where the trench stops near the prior-ABS tie, is a field call. We can't settle it from the drawings.

**2. Reconcile the two schedules**
The recovery doc lists a known gap: VDC has a Jan 4 – Feb 11, 2027 schedule, and the canonical plan has 81.5 working days. Their scope and occupancy assumptions were never compared. You decided the canonical schedule governs, so this would only document why the two differ. It doesn't change anything. S1 and S3 durations are also still "not calculated" in the Explorer.

**3. Continue the CIE implementation plan**
Milestones 1–5 (kernel, Meydenbauer adapter, scenarios, Blender/GLB bridge, Explorer) are largely in place from #35 and #37. The next milestone not yet built is **Workstream F (the 84-second decision film driven from canonical state)** or **G (a second project to show the core isn't specific to Meydenbauer)**. Highland is the obvious candidate for G. Either one is a multi-PR effort.

I'd do 0 and 1 now, because they're quick and make the B-101 frames usable, then choose between 3G and 3F based on whether the next goal is a client deliverable (F) or making the platform work beyond one project (G). Should I start on the B-101 annotations?

+The P1 corridor scene is handed over as `p1.glb`. The published interactive model predates the P1 view; `uv run bm run highland/water viewer` builds a copy that includes it. It comes from P2.2 (September 28, 2006, reference only / separate permit); plan XY is provisional and pipe heights are assumed. `P1-trace-review.html` is built by the product but not handed over here.
## What is documented, provisional and assumed
- **Documented:** building floor datums (A3.11: P1 342.00 ft, R1 353.00 ft); pipe sizes and connection patterns from P3.02/P4.01.

-- **Provisional:** Unit 107 and P1 plan XY (structural-grid calibration, ±1% scale, ±6 in local trace). Unit 107 ceilings: band-beam soffit 351.21 ft less the A7.63 drops gives living/dining 102.5 in, hallway 98.5 in, laundry 92.5 in above the P1 floor. RFI 99, ASI 54, RFI 245, RFI 344, RFI 201 and RFI 366 revised these conditions; their responses were not supplied and govern.

+- **Provisional:** Unit 107 and P1 plan XY (structural-grid calibration, ±1% scale, ±6 in local trace). Unit 107 ceilings: band-beam soffit 351.21 ft less the A7.63 drops gives living/dining 102.5 in, hallway 98.5 in, laundry 92.5 in above the P1 floor. RFI 99, ASI 54, RFI 245, RFI 344, RFI 201 and RFI 366 revised these conditions; their responses will not be supplied, so these derived heights are the working basis and remain provisional.

- **Assumed:** overhead pipe heights CW 108 / HW 106 / HWC 104 in, held inside the 102.5–109.56 in ceiling-to-soffit band (a constraint, not a measurement; no drawing gives pipe elevations); building stack XY; fixture and equipment envelopes; fittings, stops and wall-side offsets.
- **Unresolved:** the dishwasher supply connection (omitted), the 04 stack R1 continuation, and the exact P1-to-P4.01 tie-in.
- Domestic water only; sanitary, vent and gas are not modeled.

- P1 XY uses independent shared-grid fits on A2.02 and P2.2, approximately 1.5 working pixels/inch. Maximum grid-pick residual is 4.77 inches on P2.2 and 2.25 inches on A2.02; local route trace allowance is ±6 inches. P1 covers only the south corridor mains and Unit 107 approach. Its exact P4.01 tie-in, other P1 services, and actual pipe elevations are unresolved.

- Unit plan XY uses **0.51398349 inch per normalized pixel**, replacing the arbitrary 0.4. Dimensions between common grids 6–10 on A2.03 total 1,236 inches; P2.02 measures 927 PDF points, giving 0.75 point/inch. Independent E–H spans agree within 0.6%. A similarity registration transfers this scale from P2.02 to the enlarged P4.01 crop (21 inliers; median residual 0.224 PDF point). Working allowances: ±1% scale, ±6 inches local simplified trace; these are conservative allowances, not survey accuracy.

-- Unit 107 ceilings (provisional, `calibration.json` → `unit_107_ceiling`): R1 top of slab 353.0 ft, bottom of slab 351.88 ft, band-beam soffits 351.21 ft (R1-B11–B14, S3.8 det. 19/20) and 351.13 ft (R1-B7/B9, S3.7 det. 15). A7.63 measures drops from the lower of slab or drop slab, so from 351.21 ft: living/dining −8 in → **102.5 in**, hallway plenum −12 in → **98.5 in**, laundry/mechanical −18 in → **92.5 in** above the P1 floor (342.00 ft). A7.63 gives each drop as ±; master WIC is shaded low-dropped without a dimension. RFI 99, ASI 54, RFI 245 (ceiling heights), RFI 344, RFI 201 and RFI 366 revised these conditions; their responses were not supplied and govern.

+- Unit 107 ceilings (provisional, `calibration.json` → `unit_107_ceiling`): R1 top of slab 353.0 ft, bottom of slab 351.88 ft, band-beam soffits 351.21 ft (R1-B11–B14, S3.8 det. 19/20) and 351.13 ft (R1-B7/B9, S3.7 det. 15). A7.63 measures drops from the lower of slab or drop slab, so from 351.21 ft: living/dining −8 in → **102.5 in**, hallway plenum −12 in → **98.5 in**, laundry/mechanical −18 in → **92.5 in** above the P1 floor (342.00 ft). A7.63 gives each drop as ±; master WIC is shaded low-dropped without a dimension. RFI 99, ASI 54, RFI 245 (ceiling heights), RFI 344, RFI 201 and RFI 366 revised these conditions. Their responses will not be supplied (owner, 2026-11-05), so the A7.63 derivation is the working basis; it stays provisional and does not represent the revised conditions.

- Unit overhead pipe elevations are **assumed** at 108 inches CW, 106 inches HW and 104 inches HWC (previously 102/100/98, which put HWC below the derived ceilings), with 6 inches below floor for the island route. `prepare_spec.py` fails if any overhead unit run (centerline ± half nominal bore) leaves the 102.5–109.56 inch band between the highest derived ceiling and the lowest documented soffit. No drawing gives water-pipe elevations; the band is a constraint, not a measurement. P1 corridor runs use the same heights; corridor ceilings are not derived. Fixture drops, body dimensions and connecting hardware are representative.

- Building floor elevations (feet): P2 332.00, P1 342.00, R1 353.00, R2 363.25, R3 373.50, R4 383.75, R5 394.25. Model Z uses P2 as zero. The upper guide is **PLATE 404.42**, not a uniform roof. A3.11 shows other roof/plate elevations too.

- A3.11 interval notes include (+1/4 inch) additions that do not exactly match the decimal elevation differences. The model follows labeled elevations and preserves this discrepancy for clarification.

- All vertices and terminal routes in the building, unit and P1 distribution graphs reach their own system root. Tees on straight segments are recognized. Separate-system reachability does not validate hydraulic sizing, plant internals, cross-system return flow or source interpretation.

- Cycles CPU renders inspected in plan, front, side and isometric views. Orange provenance renders identify the assumed spatial geometry. Owner-color views identify systems, not provenance. Review PNGs were checked for blank output.

- Unit A and P1 model-projected overlays visually reviewed against their source crops. The P1 overlay caught and corrected a corridor-band placement error before delivery. Grid calibration, registration residuals and seven floor datums are checked automatically. Pipe routes remain simplified traces, not field-verified alignment. A bathroom close-up was also inspected.
-- Standalone HTML was previously tested with the three original GLBs. The new P1 GLB has been exported, but the viewer has not been updated or retested to include it.

+- The standalone HTML built by the `viewer` step embeds all four GLBs (Unit 107, building, plant, P1); the copy on the `highland-water-2026-11-04` release predates P1 and has only the first three. P1 is a fourth view framed on its water mains. It was tested in headless Chromium at desktop and phone widths: all four views load with no console errors, and selecting a P1 main shows its P2.2 source and provisional/assumed status.

-The full set now supplies the P1 architectural plan/RCP and a reference-only P1 plumbing plan. Resolve the dishwasher connection and return-loop details. Establish shaft positions before placing the risers spatially. If the objective is the actual installed system, confirm routes and equipment with field records/photos. Extend to other P1 services, other units and sanitary/vent/gas only after the pilot geometry is checked.

=== water
kind: model+viewer
description: "Unit 107 domestic-water pipe model from P3.02/P4.01, 3D viewer and review"
deliverables: ../../deliverables/water
steps:
  p1-sources: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/prepare_p1_sources.py
  register-p1: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/register_p1.py
  prepare: [python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/prepare_spec.py]
  build: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/build.py
  viewer:
    - cd $BM_PRODUCT_DIR && npm install && npm run bundle
    - cd $BM_PRODUCT_DIR && python package_viewer.py && python make_review.py
  # needs Playwright Chromium (installed by the script) and FFmpeg
  video: bash $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/make_video.sh
  # regenerate the committed spec from the committed calibration/source data and require no diff
  check: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/prepare_spec.py && git diff --exit-code -- $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/highland-water.spec.json
# Highland domestic-water model study

This replaces the earlier sheet-stack approach with editable pipe, equipment and fixture geometry. Start review with **Unit A / 107**, then its drawing overlay. The building and boiler views are supporting system studies. A separate **P1** scene traces the south residential corridor and Unit 107 service approach from P2.2, registered to A2.02 through shared structural grids. Unit 107 and P1 plan XY are provisional, Unit 107 ceiling heights are provisionally derived from the structural set and the unit RCP, pipe elevations remain assumed (held inside the derived ceiling-to-soffit band), and building floor datums follow A3.11. This is not a dimensionally coordinated model or a verified representation of installed conditions.

## Reproduce

Python 3.11 with `bpy==5.0.1`, PyMuPDF, Pillow and OpenCV (only for re-running source registration); Node with the pinned dependencies in package.json.

```bash
python projects/highland/products/water/register_source.py  # optional: reproduce saved Unit 107 registration
python projects/highland/products/water/prepare_p1_sources.py  # optional: requires the local full-set PDF
python projects/highland/products/water/register_p1.py
python projects/highland/products/water/prepare_spec.py
python projects/highland/products/water/build.py
cd projects/highland/products/water
npm install
npm run bundle
python package_viewer.py
python make_review.py
```

The same sequence runs as product steps from the repo root: `uv run bm run highland/water build`, then `viewer`, then `video` (film, preview GIF and viewer preview PNGs; needs FFmpeg and the system libraries Playwright's Chromium links against).

Outputs go to `build/highland-water/`. `prepare_spec.py` is the manual takeoff / presentation-coordinate definition. Its expanded `highland-water.spec.json` is the single input used for geometry, connectivity checks and drawing overlay. All dimensional values are inches; Blender uses meters internally. This project uses a dedicated builder because the repository's house extractor does not support scanned multistory plumbing plans. It is not wired into the existing house-model CI workflow.

## Sources and interpretation

- User-supplied **RL–REVISED Highland Condos Plumbing 10-29-07.pdf**, original issue October 29, 2007. Source manifest records the SHA-256.
- P3.02, PDF page 13: domestic-water riser diagram and detail 1, low-temperature boiler piping. Detail 1 explicitly has no scale.
- P4.01, PDF page 15: Unit A / 107 domestic water plan. The source crop is preserved in `source-review/unit-a.png`.
- Architectural excerpt: **Pages from 200 W. Highland Construction Plans - Complete.pdf**, 11 sheets. A2.03 (uploaded page 1) and A3.11 (uploaded page 9), both dated April 2, 2007, supply structural-grid dimensions and floor elevations. See `calibration.json` and `source-manifest.json`. The excerpt begins at R1 and does not include the P1 architectural unit plan.
- Full construction set: **200 W. Highland Construction Plans - Complete.pdf**, 190 scanned pages. A2.02 (page 46, April 2, 2007) supplies P1 architecture; P2.2 (page 183, September 28, 2006) supplies the P1 plumbing trace and is marked **reference only / separate permit**. The newer October 2007 P4.01 remains governing for Unit 107 internal routing.
- Structural set: **Structural Plans - 200 W Highland - 4.02.07.pdf** (Perbix Bykonen, 24 pages, April 2, 2007). S2.3 (page 4) R1 plan, S3.4 (page 14) PT beam schedule, S3.7 (page 17) and S3.8 (page 18) sections give the R1 slab and band-beam soffit elevations over P1.
- **A7.63** (full set page 126), RCP: Unit 107, April 2, 2007, Addendum 1 May 1, 2007: ceiling drops measured from the drop-slab soffit.
- **Plumbing - 200 W Highland - 9.28.06.pdf** (11 pages) is a lower-resolution OCR copy of full-set pages 176–186; it adds searchable text but no P3/P4 sheets and no water-pipe elevations.
- Review annotations help identify stack groups; they do not establish installed conditions or a new governing issue date.
- Building terminal groups: 01 = 5; 02 = 5; 03 = 4; 04 = 4; 05 = 5. The 04 group's R1 dwelling continuation is unresolved. Unit 106 / 107 is a separate paired continuation.
- Unit A symbols: 3 WCs, 4 lavatories, 2 showers, 1 tub, 1 kitchen sink, 1 dishwasher, 1 washer box, 1 hose bib. The washer body is only a representative context envelope for WB1. The dishwasher supply connection remains unresolved and is omitted. The 2006 reference-only P1.1 fixture schedule lists P-7A dishwasher as ½ inch HW only, no CW; its tie-in point is not shown.

## Assumptions and omissions
=== repipe
kind: viewer+film
description: "Proposed parallel-install, unit-by-unit cutover sequence (interactive page and MP4)"
deliverables: ../../deliverables/repipe
# prepare.py and package.py read the water spec and build/highland-water/unit.glb
depends_on: [highland/water]
steps:
  prepare: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/prepare.py
  # needs build/highland-water/unit.glb (water build step) and the water product's npm install
  package:
    - cd $BM_PRODUCT_DIR && NODE_PATH=../water/node_modules ../water/node_modules/.bin/esbuild app.js --bundle --minify --format=iife --outfile=app.bundle.js
    - python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/package.py
  # needs Playwright Chromium (installed by the script) and FFmpeg
  video: bash $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/make_video.sh
  check: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/prepare.py && git diff --exit-code -- $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/repipe-strategy.json
# Highland: proposed unit-by-unit repipe sequence

The owner selected **new supply routes installed alongside the existing system, followed by one-unit-at-a-time cutover**. This animation illustrates that strategy with the Unit 107 drawing study and its five-fixture bathroom pilot. It is a proposal for discussion, not a contractor-approved means-and-methods plan or a verified survey of installed piping.

## What moves

1. A representative floor-protection area appears at the bathroom pilot.
2. New distribution routes grow alongside the gray drawing reference.
3. Branches extend toward fixtures; nine pilot tie points remain disconnected.
4. The animation pauses at a testing/acceptance gate. It does not report a passed test.
5. During the scheduled cutover, nine ties switch in five fixture groups. The displayed unit boundary must be established in the field; this model does not prove independent unit isolation.
6. Service verification follows. Moving color markers indicate the sequence, not a flow or temperature simulation.
7. Only pilot terminal references fade. Shared mains stay visible because their other users are not established. The sequence then points to the next unit.

The illustration includes 37 concept routes reused from the Unit 107 domestic-water topology. Only the bathroom's nine fixture connections are explicit in the cutover demonstration. Other Unit 107 connections, shared building risers, plant interfaces and subsequent units need separate design and isolation planning. The animation is not evidence that those connections are resolved.

## Separate proposal and reference

`repipe-strategy.json` is the sequencing specification, generated by `prepare.py`. It records the reference-spec hash, owner-selected strategy, phase timing, route IDs, nine fixture ports and every assumption. The drawing-reference model remains unchanged. The viewer places reference and proposed geometry in separate scene groups; it does not relabel the reference as a verified as-built.

Every proposed route, tie point and protection graphic is **assumed**. Reference topology is reused to explain the sequence, not selected as final replacement routing. New paths are separated by **0.25 m for graphical legibility only**, not a proposed construction offset or verified clearance. Nominal diameters are enlarged 1.5× with a minimum display radius of 10 mm. Pipe sizes, materials, fittings, isolation points, access openings, protection/staging/egress limits and shutdown duration remain to be established. There are no construction quantities, test-pressure prescriptions or promises of uninterrupted service.

P4.01 supplies the underlying Unit A/107 reference. A2.03 and A3.11 support the prior grid calibration and floor datums. The original plumbing PDF annotations identify systems, risers and a floor-protection annotation on another sheet; no documented repipe method was found in the reviewed annotations/model notes. These documents are source evidence, not instructions to perform work.

## Reproduce

The water product supplies the Node dependencies (`projects/highland/products/water/package.json`: Three.js, esbuild, Playwright) and `build/highland-water/unit.glb`. Run its `build` and `viewer` steps first; the video step also needs FFmpeg. From the repo root:

```bash
uv run bm run highland/repipe prepare   # repipe-strategy.json
uv run bm run highland/repipe package   # bundle app.js, then build/highland-repipe/Highland-repipe-sequence.html
uv run bm run highland/repipe video     # browser checks, MP4, preview GIF, cutover still, validation.json
```

`make_video.sh` serves `build/highland-repipe/`, runs `render.cjs`, cuts the preview GIF from the full 32 s at 6 fps and 800 px, copies the phase-5 capture to `Cutover-preview.png`, fully decodes the MP4 and fails if the decoded frame count differs. To run only the browser checks and review stills, serve the folder and run `node projects/highland/products/repipe/render.cjs <url> build/highland-repipe --review-only` with `NODE_PATH` set to the water product's `node_modules`.

The standalone HTML offers Play/Pause, a time slider, and seven phase buttons. The 32-second video is 1280×720 at 24 fps.

## Checks and limits

=== installation
kind: model+film
description: "Proposed repipe installation method model, 90-second film, immersive and studio cuts"
deliverables: ../../deliverables/installation
assets: release-assets.json
steps:
  restore: bm assets pull $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/release-assets.json
  validate: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/installation/validate_installation.py
  build: [cd $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/installation && python build_installation.py && python verify_blends.py,
          cd $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/installation && python package_installation.py && python validate_installation.py]
check_unavailable: "validation needs Highland-original.pdf and the .blend models restored from the LFS assets (bm run highland/installation restore); CI does not fetch LFS in build-models"
# 200 W Highland — installation models and 90-second animation

**Current presentation:** [Full-frame architectural cut and editable titles](immersive-film/README.md) · [Watch the complete 90-second review](../../deliverables/installation/immersive-film/Highland-repipe-immersive-90s-1080p.mp4).

[Studio revision: exterior opening, depth, cameras and callouts](studio-upgrade/README.md) · [Revised film and upgrade guide](../../deliverables/installation/studio-upgrade/README.md)

The proposed CPVC replacement sequence follows shared distribution into the **Unit B / 106 pilot**, then shows verification, access, new distribution, branches, testing, service transfer and restoration. This is a separate pilot from the earlier Unit A / 107 strategy study in `projects/highland/products/repipe/`.

[Watch or download the films and editable models](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/releases/tag/highland-repipe-2026-10-17) · [Eight-frame preview](../../deliverables/installation/README.md)

The delivery contains the 90-second 4K and 1080p H.264 movies, eight-page storyboard, editable animation package and original installation-model package. Git contains the governing specifications, scripts, source crops, individual storyboard frames and review evidence. The five large downloads use **Git LFS** in `projects/highland/deliverables/installation/assets/`; the release page links to those files. `release-assets.json` records their sizes and SHA-256 hashes.

## Source and status

- [Installation specification](installation/highland-installation-proposed.yaml) governs the proposed geometry. Every new physical element is **assumed**; source drawings establish relationships, not measured installation dimensions.
- [Existing-reference specification](installation/highland-installation-existing-reference.yaml) remains separate. The user's report of failing CPVC does not establish surveyed existing routes.
- [Animation specification](animation-90s/animation-spec.json) governs the exact eight-shot, 90-second timeline. Flow markers begin only after the depicted transfer.
- [Source manifest](source-manifest.json) records the supplied 19-sheet plumbing set issued 29 October 2007. P3.02 supplies the shared schematic; P4.01 supplies Unit B / 106 context. Unit 101 irrigation and Unit 302 alternate-wall notes require separate review.

The source title says 200 West Highland; its location block says 202 W Highland. That discrepancy and the governing revision remain unresolved. The models establish no verified pipe sizes, material selection, isolation boundaries, opening dimensions, hydraulic performance, test results or shutdown duration. Fixture symbols represent groups rather than verified individual counts.

## Restore the editable project

Use Python 3.11 and Git LFS, with GitHub access to this private repository. Run these commands from the repository root:

```bash
uv run bm assets pull projects/highland/products/installation/release-assets.json
```

With Git LFS installed (`git lfs pull --include='projects/highland/deliverables/installation/assets/*'`) the committed copies are used; otherwise the assets are downloaded from the `highland-repipe-2026-10-17` release with `gh`.

The restoration script verifies both archives before writing, restores the original PDF, Blender/GLB models, PDFs, short installation movie and audio stems, and preserves modified local assets by refusing to overwrite them. It leaves tracked source files intact. The two 90-second movie masters remain in the delivery assets folder. To use ZIPs downloaded through GitHub's **Download raw file** button instead, add `--from <their directory>`.

Open `animation-90s/Highland-repipe-90s.blend` at **MASTER - 90 seconds**. Its two source-derived 3D scenes, camera keyframes, construction reveals, native graphics and relative audio/image references remain editable. Keep the folder structure intact. The original installation Blender files remain separate and unchanged.

## Rebuild and verify

FFmpeg/FFprobe and the DejaVu Sans regular/bold fonts are system prerequisites. `uv sync --group vision --group pdf` (from the repo root) installs Python 3.11 and the locked dependencies; the generic house/detail builder does not implement this plumbing-method model.

```bash
=== walkthrough
kind: films
description: "Lobby-to-corridor walkthrough: browser drone tour, native Blender film, archviz stills and the RunPod cinema cut"
deliverables: [../../deliverables/drone, ../../deliverables/blender-film, ../../deliverables/archviz]
# prepare.py (the check) reads exterior/exterior.spec.json
depends_on: [highland/exterior]
steps:
  drone: bash $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/build.sh
  preview: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/blender_preview.py --samples 8 --width 270 --height 480
  cinema-assets: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/cinema_assets.py
  runpod-cinema: bash $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/runpod_render.sh
  check: python $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/prepare.py && git diff --exit-code -- $BM_PRODUCT_DIR/flight.spec.json
# Highland lobby-to-corridor drone view

A 26-second, portrait flight for a phone: the camera approaches the east facade, crosses the broad glazed entrance of Lobby 110, follows its connector into Corridor 108, enters an illustrative elevator, rises to R2, and continues down Corridor 208 toward the stair. An interactive, self-contained HTML viewer has Play/Pause and scrubbing; the MP4 uses the same camera path and adds a synthesized stereo score. The walkthrough is a presentation study of public circulation, not an as-built interior survey.

## Basis

- `../exterior/exterior.spec.json` and its GLB establish the exterior footprint, R1 level and the east `east-R1-08` entry opening. This opening is classified **entry** in the model; A2.03 shows lobby glazing/doors there. The flight does not assert a separate operable window.
- Architectural sheets **A2.03 and A2.04**, dated 04-02-07, locate **Lobby 110**, **Corridors 108/208**, two elevators, and Stair M1. A2.03 labels the core corridor at **6 ft**. A3.11 supplies R1/R2 floor elevations 353.00/363.25 ft, a 10 ft 3 in rise. The PDF SHA-256 is in `flight.spec.json`; high-resolution crops are in `source-review/`.
- The lobby, connector and long corridor rectangles in `flight.spec.json` are manually fitted to the plans and rounded. They use the exterior study's plan-coordinate system in inches. The six-foot R1 width is documented; R2 reuse and exact wall faces are provisional. The path and test points are recorded in feet for readability.

The existing exterior GLB contains no real interior partitions. Floors, walls, ceiling (assumed 8 ft 6 in clear), doors, elevator cab/fronts, stair door, fixtures, lighting and finishes in this tour are **illustrative**. A short dark transition at the glazing covers the switch to the plan-based interior. The vertical rise is documented, while the elevator car and door timing are not. This model does not depict residential unit interiors, concealed plumbing or an egress survey. The entry doors open with camera proximity; the elevator doors use the presentation timing. The gold ribbon traces the camera route, not a construction or accessible route. Upper-floor window illumination, tree motion, the external glass/brass elevator section, and warm area lights are visual treatments. The owner selected **new supply routes installed alongside the existing system, followed by one-unit-at-a-time cutover**. This animation illustrates that strategy with the Unit 107 drawing study and its five-fixture bathroom pilot. It is a proposal for discussion, not a contractor-approved means-and-methods plan or a verified survey of installed piping.

## What moves

1. A representative floor-protection area appears at the bathroom pilot.
2. New distribution routes grow alongside the gray drawing reference.
3. Branches extend toward fixtures; nine pilot tie points remain disconnected.
4. The animation pauses at a testing/acceptance gate. It does not report a passed test.
5. During the scheduled cutover, nine ties switch in five fixture groups. The displayed unit boundary must be established in the field; this model does not prove independent unit isolation.
6. Service verification follows. Moving color markers indicate the sequence, not a flow or temperature simulation.
7. Only pilot terminal references fade. Shared mains stay visible because their other users are not established. The sequence then points to the next unit.

The illustration includes 37 concept routes reused from the Unit 107 domestic-water topology. Only the bathroom's nine fixture connections are explicit in the cutover demonstration. Other Unit 107 connections, shared building risers, plant interfaces and subsequent units need separate design and isolation planning. The animation is not evidence that those connections are resolved.

## Separate proposal and reference

`repipe-strategy.json` is the sequencing specification, generated by `prepare.py`. It records the reference-spec hash, owner-selected strategy, phase timing, route IDs, nine fixture ports and every assumption. The drawing-reference model remains unchanged. The viewer places reference and proposed geometry in separate scene groups; it does not relabel the reference as a verified as-built.

Every proposed route, tie point and protection graphic is **assumed**. Reference topology is reused to explain the sequence, not selected as final replacement routing. New paths are separated by **0.25 m for graphical legibility only**, not a proposed construction offset or verified clearance. Nominal diameters are enlarged 1.5× with a minimum display radius of 10 mm. Pipe sizes, materials, fittings, isolation points, access openings, protection/staging/egress limits and shutdown duration remain to be established. There are no construction quantities, test-pressure prescriptions or promises of uninterrupted service.

P4.01 supplies the underlying Unit A/107 reference. A2.03 and A3.11 support the prior grid calibration and floor datums. The original plumbing PDF annotations identify systems, risers and a floor-protection annotation on another sheet; no documented repipe method was found in the reviewed annotations/model notes. - **Highland-repipe-immersive-90s-1080p.mp4** — the complete 90-second cut, 1920 × 1080 at 24 fps, with the approved narration/score and optional selectable narration captions.

The saved master uses the clean model movie as its picture layer. Edit the retained 3D scenes and re-render them when changing modeled work. Source geometry, original sequencing and field-verification requirements are preserved; graphic arrival glimmers do not depict water flow. # Model from drawings or photos

Follow `docs/METHOD.md` (rules) and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (exact commands). This is the order and the gates.

## 0. Orient
```bash
uv run bm doctor          # need: bpy for builds; sources present for intake
uv run bm list --json     # does the site already exist? which specs?
```
If bpy is missing locally, you can still write and validate specs (`bm check`), and CI builds them.

## 1. Site
New jobsite: `uv run bm new <site> --type element|detail --name "<display name>"`, then fill
`projects/<site>/project.yaml` (address, building type, scope). Put source PDFs/photos in
`projects/<site>/sources/` (never committed) and inventory each one in `sources/manifest.json`
(file, sha256, sheet ids, revision/date, scale, photo ids).

## 2. Pick the model type
- **detail**: one section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) → start from `templates/project/specs/detail.yaml`;
  example `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-rake-ah700-12.yaml`.
- **house**: plan-extracted shell + takeoff → RUNBOOK steps 2–11; example `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-cottage-a.yaml`.
- **element**: boxes per member (framing bay, deck) → `templates/project/specs/element.yaml`.
- **room**: photo-only interior → `projects/room-living-kitchen/specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml`.
- Existing condition and proposed repair → two specs (`<x>-existing.yaml`, `<x>-proposed.yaml`).

## 3. Takeoff into the spec (gates)
- Calibrate each sheet from its own dimension strings (`uv run bm calibrate scale …`); never trust the title block.
- Every element: `confirmed` + `source` (dimension on a document), `provisional` + `source` + how measured and
  tolerance, or `assumed` + `basis`. Actual lumber sizes. Never scale an NTS detail.
- Add document-driven `checks` (counts, overall extents, gaps, elevations) each with a `source`.
- Conflicting sources: model the governing one, write the conflict into `flags:`.

## 4. Build and verify
```bash
uv run bm check --no-tests                     # provenance errors without bpy
uv run bm build <site>/<spec> --no-render       # checks only, seconds
uv run bm build <site>/<spec>                   # + review renders in build/<site>/<spec>/
```
Read `build/<site>/<spec>/report.md`, then **look at** the review PNGs (plan/front/side/iso, provenance
colors). Where an elevation exists: `uv run bm overlay …` (RUNBOOK step 10) and report the edge agreement.
No local bpy: push a branch and read the `build-models` run instead.

## 5. Report back
State: checks passed (n/n), renders looked at (which), overlays (agreement %), every assumed element, and
what is not modeled. Never call provisional or assumed geometry documented.


ARGUMENTS: highland: building domestic-water risers + mains (P3.02 riser diagram, P2/P-level plans), proposed PEX-A replacement, existing vs proposed separate specs; feeds a photoreal RunPod visualization of opening, install, cutover and restoration.
Next I'll check what this machine can run and whether the governing plumbing set and the photos are in `sources/`.

import json
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
SOURCE = HERE.parents[3] / "build/highland-water/p1-source"
OUT = HERE / "source-review"

# Manually picked shared grid intersections on the 144-dpi working rasters.
# X distances are from grid 7; Y distances are from grid E, positive upward.
plumbing_grids = {
    "x": {"7": 3142, "8": 3642, "9": 4146, "10": 4694},
    "y": {"E": 2386, "F": 2712, "G": 3158, "H": 3427},
}
architecture_grids = {
    "x": {"6": 2880, "7": 3168, "8": 3673, "9": 4173, "10": 4744},
    "y": {"E": 2402, "F": 2728, "G": 3165, "H": 3431},
}
x_distances = {"6": -195, "7": 0, "8": 333, "9": 666, "10": 1041}
y_distances = {"E": 0, "F": -216, "G": -510, "H": -690}

def fit_axis(pixels, distances):
    names = list(pixels)
    design = np.array([[pixels[name], 1] for name in names])
    values = np.array([distances[name] for name in names])
    scale, offset = np.linalg.lstsq(design, values, rcond=None)[0]
    predicted = design @ np.array([scale, offset])
    return {
        "names": names,
        "working_px": [pixels[name] for name in names],
        "distance_in": [distances[name] for name in names],
        "in_per_working_px": float(scale),
        "offset_in": float(offset),
        "residual_in": (predicted - values).tolist(),
    }

result = {
    "method": "Least-squares registration of manually picked shared structural grids; no title-block scale used",
    "source": "P2.2, full-set PDF page 183, 09-28-06, reference only / separate permit",
    "target": "A2.02, full-set PDF page 46, 04-02-07",
    "working_pixels_per_pdf_point": 2.0,
    "status": "provisional",
    "plumbing": {
        "x": fit_axis(plumbing_grids["x"], x_distances),
        "y": fit_axis(plumbing_grids["y"], y_distances),
    },
    "architecture": {
        "x": fit_axis(architecture_grids["x"], x_distances),
        "y": fit_axis(architecture_grids["y"], y_distances),
    },
}
for sheet in ("plumbing", "architecture"):
    px_per_in = 1 / result[sheet]["x"]["in_per_working_px"]
    py_per_in = -1 / result[sheet]["y"]["in_per_working_px"]
    result[sheet]["working_px_per_in"] = [float(px_per_in), float(py_per_in)]
    result[sheet]["max_grid_residual_in"] = float(max(
        abs(v) for axis in ("x", "y") for v in result[sheet][axis]["residual_in"]
    ))

# X distances are from grid 7; Y distances are from grid E, positive upward.
plumbing_grids = {
    "x": {"7": 3142, "8": 3642, "9": 4146, "10": 4694},
    "y": {"E": 2386, "F": 2712, "G": 3158, "H": 3427},
}
architecture_grids = {
    "x": {"6": 2880, "7": 3168, "8": 3673, "9": 4173, "10": 4744},
    "y": {"E": 2402, "F": 2728, "G": 3165, "H": 3431},
}
x_distances = {"6": -195, "7": 0, "8": 333, "9": 666, "10": 1041}
y_distances = {"E": 0, "F": -216, "G": -510, "H": -690}

def fit_axis(pixels, distances):
    names = list(pixels)
    design = np.array([[pixels[name], 1] for name in names])
    values = np.array([distances[name] for name in names])
    scale, offset = np.linalg.lstsq(design, values, rcond=None)[0]
    predicted = design @ np.array([scale, offset])
    return {
        "names": names,
        "working_px": [pixels[name] for name in names],
        "distance_in": [distances[name] for name in names],
        "in_per_working_px": float(scale),
        "offset_in": float(offset),
        "residual_in": (predicted - values).tolist(),
    }

result = {
    "method": "Least-squares registration of manually picked shared structural grids; no title-block scale used",
    "source": "P2.2, full-set PDF page 183, 09-28-06, reference only / separate permit",
    "target": "A2.02, full-set PDF page 46, 04-02-07",
    "working_pixels_per_pdf_point": 2.0,
    "status": "provisional",
    "plumbing": {
        "x": fit_axis(plumbing_grids["x"], x_distances),
        "y": fit_axis(plumbing_grids["y"], y_distances),
    },
    "architecture": {
        "x": fit_axis(architecture_grids["x"], x_distances),
        "y": fit_axis(architecture_grids["y"], y_distances),
    },
}
for sheet in ("plumbing", "architecture"):
    px_per_in = 1 / result[sheet]["x"]["in_per_working_px"]
    py_per_in = -1 / result[sheet]["y"]["in_per_working_px"]
    result[sheet]["working_px_per_in"] = [float(px_per_in), float(py_per_in)]
    result[sheet]["max_grid_residual_in"] = float(max(

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it.
